seoTitle: Add a Logo and Favicon Icon to Squarespace (2026)
metaDescription: Learn how to upload a logo and set a custom browser icon in Squarespace, so your header and browser tab both show your brand from day one.
intro: If you're launching or redesigning a Squarespace site, your logo and browser icon are two of the first branding details visitors notice. This guide walks through uploading a logo to your site header and setting a matching favicon so your tab icon reflects your brand too.

steps.heading: Log in and choose your site
steps.body: Sign in to your Squarespace account (Continue with Google works if that's how your account is linked), then select the website you want to update from your dashboard.

steps.heading: Open the site header editor
steps.body: From the dashboard, click Edit or Configure to enter the site editor, then locate Edit Site Header to access your branding controls.

steps.heading: Upload your logo
steps.body: In the Site Title & Logo section, click the pencil icon to edit, then choose Add Image and upload a high-resolution PNG or SVG. It appears in your header immediately after uploading.

steps.heading: Set the browser icon (favicon)
steps.body: Go to Design and select Browser Icon (on 7.1, search 'favicon' in the dashboard search bar). Upload a square image at least 100x100 pixels in PNG, ICO, JPG, or SVG format.

steps.heading: Save and verify
steps.body: Click Save, then clear your browser cache and refresh your site to confirm the new logo and favicon are showing correctly.

faq.question: What image format should I use for a Squarespace logo?
faq.answer: A high-resolution PNG or SVG works best, since both preserve transparency and stay sharp at different header sizes.

faq.question: Why isn't my new favicon showing up?
faq.answer: Browsers cache favicons aggressively. Clear your cache or open the site in an incognito window to see the update.

faq.question: Does the favicon need to be a specific size?
faq.answer: Squarespace requires a square image at least 100 by 100 pixels, saved as PNG, ICO, JPG, or SVG.

faq.question: Can I use the same image for both the logo and favicon?
faq.answer: You can, but since the favicon displays very small in the browser tab, a simplified icon version of your logo usually looks clearer than the full logo.
